Reviewed the diff against `app/controllers/kraken_items_controller.rb` and the test. Confirmed:

- The fix is byte-for-byte the same shape as sibling PR #4276 (CoinSpot), and matches the already-merged pattern in `PlaidItemsController#render_frame_redirect`, `CoinbaseItemsController#render_frame_redirect`, and `BinanceItemsController#render_frame_redirect` on `main`. The `turbo_frame_request?` branch, the `flash[:alert]` + `turbo_frame_tag(turbo_frame_request_id) { turbo_stream.action(:redirect, path) }` body, and the non-frame `redirect_to` fallback are all consistent with that precedent, so this is low-risk.
- The new test exercises the real regression (frame request getting a 302 instead of the redirect stream) and asserts both the `turbo-stream[action=redirect]` markup and the flash message; `kraken_items.select_accounts.select_connection` does exist in `config/locales/views/kraken_items/en.yml`, so the key reference is valid. No tenancy/authorization concerns — `select_accounts` only reads from `kraken_item_account_flow_context`, which is already scoped to `Current.family`, and this change doesn't touch that scoping.
- One thing worth a follow-up (not blocking this PR): `render_frame_redirect` is now duplicated verbatim across five controllers (Plaid, Coinbase, Binance, CoinSpot, and now Kraken), same body and same comment. Given AGENTS.md's push to keep controllers thin, this is a good candidate to hoist into a shared concern (e.g. something like `TurboFrameRedirectable`) the next time one of these provider controllers is touched, rather than continuing to copy-paste it per provider.

Codex and CodeRabbit already reviewed with no actionable findings, and I agree — nothing further to flag beyond the DRY note above.
